A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAS-ProVe and provide readable main texts and complete appendices. Corresponding tables, figures, methods, and appendix sections can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of six MAS frameworks on AIME24, AIME25, and GAIA, including verification, context-management, and solvability experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds HumanEval and GPQA evaluations, runtime measurements, context-sensitivity tests, generation-versus-ranking diagnostics, and beam-search results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B.4 introduce a width-3 beam-search variant for Debate alongside the existing greedy verifier-guided search. The core verification wrapper, verifier models, granularity options, and context-management procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds coding on HumanEval and scientific reasoning on GPQA, with evaluations across all six MAS frameworks in Table 2. This substantially broadens coverage beyond the retained mathematical-reasoning benchmarks and GAIA information-extraction subset.

E2.justification: v2 Table 11 adds beam search as a comparison method against Debate's unverified baseline and greedy judge-guided search. The original six MAS frameworks and five verifier models remain; their extension to HumanEval and GPQA does not itself change comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 introduces distinct diagnostic protocols: 153 fixed-candidate comparisons across context formats and 128 sampled trajectories for each of four AIME questions, followed by judging controlled correct/incorrect candidate sets. It also introduces GPT-4.1-nano for HumanEval and the width-3 beam-search condition. These supplement the retained evaluation settings.

E4.justification: New Appendices B.1-B.4 examine verification latency, context-induced ranking disagreement, generation failures versus conditional verifier success, and sensitivity to greedy versus beam search. These address diagnostic questions absent from v1. The earlier MAS-Zero scaling, context, benchmark, and case-study analyses remain as B.5-B.8.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly reports 20 repeated judging trials for its controlled ranking experiment. The original three-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and 30-trial CoT difficulty stratification remain unchanged; this does not establish increased repetition of the original experiments.

E6.justification: All nine original tables retain their numerical contents. v2 adds HumanEval/GPQA scores, latency measurements, context-format agreement rates, conditional ranking results, and beam-search scores. For example, Table 11 newly reports beam-search accuracy of 82.72±0.87 on AIME24 and 66.67±4.72 on AIME25 under the added search condition.

T1.justification: The existing difficulty, token-growth, and efficiency definitions and mathematical case study are retained. The added cost-accounting discussion is explanatory prose, and the solvability additions are empirical; no new formal theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is provided.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's main observations, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: verification is inconsistent, generative judges generally perform better, context and granularity matter, and verification mainly stabilizes already-solvable queries. The modular framework contribution is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds focused interpretations attributing degradation to context-sensitive misranking, distinguishing generation failure from conditional ranking failure, and presenting marginal beam-search gains as support for greedy search. It also adds qualifications about computational overhead and API-dependent latency. The overarching interpretation of verification's limitations remains.

D1.justification: v2 specifies GPT-4.1-nano for HumanEval, gives the beam width, and reports wall-clock runtimes with qualifications about asynchronous commercial APIs, server load, and rate limits. Existing prompt templates, implementation code, and code-access information are retained; Appendix A does not supply corresponding detailed descriptions for the two added datasets.

R1.justification: v2 adds the HumanEval reference, Chen et al. (2021), and the GPQA reference, Rein et al. (2023). Related-work positioning otherwise remains unchanged. Publication and venue updates for already-cited works do not introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: The revision makes targeted setup and results additions, inserts four appendix subsections, updates cross-references, and adds acknowledgements and conference publication text. The main section sequence, most prose, prompts, code templates, and case studies remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Appendix Tables 9-11, with localized reflow and relocation of existing displays. All twelve original figures retain their graphical content. Figure 3's caption is corrected to describe both mathematical-reasoning benchmarks already shown; the overall visual design remains.

improvement.justification: The added domains, controlled context comparisons, beam-search ablation, and latency reporting make applicability, sensitivity, and costs better assessable. These are useful gains over v1. Their overall benefit is limited by incomplete documentation of the new benchmarks and overinterpretation in B.2-B.3: ranking disagreement alone does not establish harmful misranking, and 128 sampled trajectories cannot prove a fundamental generation limit.
